name: Air Fryer Filipino Daing na Bangus with Garlic Rice and Tomato Salad

components.name: Daing na Bangus

ingredients.name: Raw DEBONED butterflied milkfish, edible fish weight excluding head and large bones

steps: For accurate scaling buy boneless cleaned bangus and weigh 880 g of edible fish, excluding head, spine and large bones. The number of whole milkfish needed depends on supplier yield.
Mix vinegar, 30 g garlic, sliced onion, salt and pepper. Refrigerate fish in marinade for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight. Discard marinade after use.

Drain and dry the fish. Brush with 20 ml oil. Air fry at 180 C for about 9-12 minutes per side depending on fish thickness and basket fit, until fish reaches 63 C. Large butterflied pieces may need portioning.
Pack four portions of fish and garlic rice. Make salad fresh for best quality. Watch closely for small pin bones even when sold deboned.

components.name: Garlic Rice
steps: Cook the measured dry rice in water and rest covered. In a pan warm the 15 ml oil and gently toast the 22 g sliced garlic until aromatic; mix through the cooked rice.

components.name: Tomato-Onion Salad
steps: Toss fresh tomatoes and onions with calamansi juice, storing salad apart from fish and rice.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Filipino air-fryer daing na bangus adapted from published vinegar-garlic marinade, with a measured garlic-rice and tomato side.
Planning: ADVANCE PREP: marinate 3 hours or overnight. SECONDARY STOVETOP garlic rice.
Freezer: garlic rice freezes if chilled promptly; cooked bangus can freeze but dry out; fresh salad NOT suitable
Dietary: Fish, possible residual pin bones; no pork.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Fish — plan for days 1-3; make the tomato salad fresh.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
